---
title: "Inspect local remote versions"
---

Current source work: ordinary local latest/archive inspection. This command does
not upload, restore, verify artifact bytes or change configured remote definitions.
It is separate from CAS and the deferred registry design.

```bash
proj --project . remote versions --path /physical/path/to/archive --label raw-data
proj --machine --project . remote versions --path /physical/path/to/latest --label raw-data --structure latest
```

Paths relative to the command's selected project root are supported. Use physical
paths: symlinked parents, candidate directories and VERSION files are rejected.
No active project config, Git credentials or remote account are required.

Archive is the default layout: base/label/version directories. Numeric versions
sort newest first, including empty variants. The actual directory path is retained
even when version spellings differ. Multiple spellings or full/empty variants
remain visible rather than silently selecting one for restore. Unrelated names
are skipped; malformed numeric-looking version names and special candidates fail.

Latest reads the exact label entry from base/VERSION. It reports the trailing
asterisk as metadata_untrusted, plus present and empty fields. A missing target is
reported explicitly; an absent asterisk is **not proof of verified content**.
Archive results do not infer trust from metadata and return null for that field.
An absent base or VERSION yields no entries and creates nothing. Duplicate label
entries and malformed advertised versions are errors.

Use --path-append-label false only when version directories or latest contents
are directly at the supplied base. VERSION remains at that explicit base.
For latest, reading that file means the base already exists, so present is true
and empty is false: a sibling base-empty is not selected. This mode does not
infer whether the base contains data files; directory presence is not integrity.
This makes the inspected path explicit; it is not a new remote registry format.

Machine output retains protocol v1 and adds a versions query result. No byte
verification, latest-source selection, credential discovery or publication occurs.

## Download one ordinary local version

Current source work adds remote download. It is an explicit transfer, independent
of configured source selection and build publication. For archive, supply the
exact numeric directory spelling via --remote-version (for example v1.2.3-4).
For latest, omit that option: the advertised VERSION label entry is required.
A full archive directory wins over its corresponding -empty variant.

```bash
proj --project . remote download --path /physical/archive --label raw-data --remote-version v1.2.3 --destination downloaded-data
proj --project . remote download --path /physical/latest --label raw-data --structure latest --destination downloaded-data
```

The destination parent must exist. Private staging receives all source files
(including nested and hidden files) before an existing destination changes.
Matching files receive downloaded bytes; destination-only files survive by
default. --clear explicitly discards those extras only after staging succeeds.
An empty source marker preserves existing files normally, or produces an empty
destination with --clear. A marker containing entries is rejected.

Project-root/ancestor, VCS/framework-state and overlapping destinations are
rejected, along with symlinked paths and linked/special copied entries. Hard-linked
external aliases keep their bytes. Copy/selection failure preserves the existing
destination. If installation fails, restoration is attempted; a failed rollback
reports where the original directory was retained. This is not crash atomicity
or protection against concurrent writers. Post-install cleanup failure is reported
as an installed download with incomplete private-staging cleanup.

The command does not authenticate metadata, compare downloaded bytes to CSV,
choose configured restore sources or change local VERSION/manifest/configuration.
A latest untrusted marker does not prevent this explicitly requested download;
it remains a warning about metadata, not a verified-content claim.
Machine mode returns completed: true only after successful completion.

Permission flags are preserved for newly downloaded entries. Merge mode retains
existing file/directory permission flags, and an existing destination root keeps
its flags even with --clear. Ownership, ACLs and extended attributes are outside
this bounded guarantee; replacing a tree is not a full metadata-preserving backup.

## Inspect and apply a concrete local file policy

Current source work adds remote store for file-inspected transfers to one
explicit physical target. This is the file-policy layer, not configured build
publication or archive/version metadata management. Supply --inspect file
explicitly; manifest/none inspection are not accepted by this bounded command.
The existing configuration default inspection is unchanged.

```bash
proj --machine --project . remote store --source generated --destination /physical/remote/output/v1.2.3 --inspect file --dry-run
proj --project . remote store --source generated --destination /physical/remote/output/v1.2.3 --inspect file --strategy sync-diff
```

The default strategy is sync-diff, matching projr. upload-all selects every
source file and keeps destination-only files; upload-missing uploads only absent
names; sync-diff uploads new/different files and removes destination-only files;
sync-purge lists all existing files for removal and every source file for upload.
A dry run reports uploads, overwrites, removals and same_bytes (informational
even when those paths are re-uploaded). It creates nothing.

This command uses current streaming MD5 byte inventories, not modification time
or a claim of authenticity. Hidden/nested files are included; empty subdirectories
are not transfer records. The destination parent must exist. It stages selected
source bytes, checks their hashes and rechecks source/target inventories before
the shared guarded installer changes the target. Mirror execution builds a full
replacement snapshot, so unchanged bytes may be copied privately too; do not
interpret the plan as a syscall or disk-I/O count.

Source files stay unchanged. Retained paths of the same type keep existing
permission flags; new paths use source flags. The download safeguards and limits
above apply, including Windows read-only cleanup failures and partial cleanup
residue. No crash/concurrent-writer isolation or ACL/ownership/xattr parity follows.

VERSION, manifest.csv, configured remotes, cue selection, historical comparison,
empty remote naming and GitHub/CAS structures are untouched. Use the concrete
version directory as destination; this command does not publish a complete
discoverable remote snapshot by itself.

Native filename aliases (for example A.csv/a.csv on a case-insensitive target)
are rejected before staging when the planned spelling differs from an existing
entry. This includes directory components and keeps upload-missing from becoming
an overwrite. Case-sensitive targets retain distinct names. Case-only migrations
are not silently inferred by this bounded file-policy command.


## Work with explicit GitHub Release assets

The source CLI provides remote github assets, remote github upload and remote
github download. Each requires --repository owner/repo and --tag RELEASE_TAG.
Upload also requires --source FILE and --name ASSET_NAME; --create-release
explicitly permits a missing Release to be created. Existing names are rejected
without deletion. Download requires --name, --destination FILE and --max-bytes N.
Source/destination file paths are relative to the selected project root unless
absolute. The destination parent must already exist.

Use an existing GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, in that order. Public list
and download requests can be anonymous. GITHUB_API_URL supports an explicit
Enterprise API endpoint including /api/v3. Tokens are never command arguments.
No authentication setup or additional credential helper is installed.

Machine assets returns result.assets; machine upload/download returns completed
through the existing worker. ZIP creation/extraction, projr metadata ZIP handling
and configured restore are not yet provided by these explicit asset commands.
An interrupted upload can have an uncertain remote result: inspect before retry.
Downloads stage complete bytes before replacement, preserve existing permissions,
and reject protected project state, links and special files. No archive integrity,
crash atomicity or concurrent-writer isolation claim follows.

The CLI does not initialise HTTP wire logging and its own error messages omit
tokens, response bodies and signed redirect URLs. Library embedders must avoid
ureq DEBUG/TRACE logging for sensitive requests because dependency logging is
not redacted. Redirects remove Authorization but do not confine network access
to a provider host; this transport is not a network sandbox.


## GitHub ZIP packaging and explicit directory transfer

Current source extends the native Release transport with projr flat names:
prefix-label-vVERSION.zip for archive, prefix-label.zip for latest, and
-empty before .zip for empty variants. With no prefix, the label is always
used, including path_append_label=false. Metadata assets remain shared and
unprefixed: manifest.zip contains manifest.csv, VERSION.zip contains VERSION,
and CHANGELOG.zip contains CHANGELOG.md. Directory ZIP entries are relative to
the selected source, without an enclosing folder. Nonempty parent-directory entries retain Unix
permission modes; empty directory entries remain omitted. Empty sources contain the
single zero-byte projr-empty sentinel; empty subdirectories are not archived.

The CLI adds remote github upload-directory (label/structure/remote-version,
optional prefix/path-append-label), upload-metadata (kind manifest/version/
changelog and a source directory), and download-directory (exact asset name,
destination, max-bytes, max-expanded-bytes, optional clear/empty). Uploads remain
new-name-only; metadata is packaged byte-for-byte rather than silently merged.
Download stages extraction privately and uses the existing guarded merge/clear
installer. Explicit empty requires exactly the sentinel and consumes it before
installation. Destination-only files survive unless clear is requested.

Safety changes from R's direct utils::unzip: bounded expanded bytes and100000
members, CRC validation, reject links/special/encrypted entries, traversal,
backslashes, device names, native aliases, duplicate members and parent/file
collisions before project installation. Retain existing installer rollback and
Windows backup-cleanup limits; no crash/concurrent-writer guarantee is added.

Ponytail full: one ZIP crate with only Deflate enabled, existing MD5 inventory,
HTTP client and guarded installer. No backend interface, registry or new YAML
policy. Independent tests cover exact metadata/Unicode/hidden/empty members,
malicious names, CRC/expanded limits and mocked actual ZIP upload/download
merge/clear. No local heavy tests; remote lock resolution, exact-head platform/
pinned/docs acceptance and independent review are pending.

[flat names](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote.R#L525),

Historical metadata merging, automatic publication, credential-helper fallback
and complete CAS-structure integration remain outstanding. This
source candidate does not update the published/installed preview.

Review amendments share the existing native directory-entry alias guard with
file-policy transfers, validate empty-directory CRC with a bounded probe, and
never persist an expanded-byte probe beyond each member's advertised size.
Directory modes apply deepest-first after extraction; an existing destination's
modes still follow the previously documented merge policy. File-only ZIPs from
other writers have no directory privacy metadata to restore. Source root modes
are not encoded as a new manifest field. No ACL/ownership/xattr claim follows.
Temporary paths are created beneath the physical canonical system temp directory;
macOS /var aliases are not an excuse to weaken external path guards.

Extraction also checks actual directory spelling immediately after creation,
rejecting filesystems that rewrite it rather than merging distinct Unicode
members. The extracted-tree owner restores directory owner access for cleanup;
explicit close reports a retained path on cleanup failure. The directory-transfer
command checks extraction and transfer cleanup on success and failure and
distinguishes installed output from failed transfer. Readonly/zero-mode owned
directory cleanup is exercised unprivileged in the pinned gate.


## Explicit GitHub asset replacement

Current source adds --replace to upload, upload-directory and upload-metadata,
and GithubReleaseClient::replace_asset. Default uploads still reject existing
names. Explicit replacement follows the working projr delete-then-upload sequence:
[remote-github-httr.R554-662](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote-github-httr.R#L554).

Before deletion, validate the regular source, stage its complete bytes privately,
resolve the Release/unique asset and validate its trusted upload endpoint. An
absent name uploads normally. A successful delete is followed by one upload;
errors after deletion explicitly state that the previous asset was deleted.
An interrupted deletion reports an uncertain old-asset state and does not start
the upload. This is not atomic publication, backup retention or remote rollback.
There is no automatic retry, new history/sealing policy or changed YAML default.

Ponytail full reuses the existing client and request/body fixtures, with a private
file snapshot only for explicit replacement. Mocked end-to-end witnesses cover
staged bytes despite source mutation after delete, exact DELETE/POST ordering,
denied/interrupted delete, failed/malformed upload, untrusted endpoints, ambiguous
names, unsafe sources and machine CLI output. These are mocked REST operations,
not actual GitHub Release mutations. No live user data/credentials or local
heavy tests. PR182 passed exact-head remote gates and independent review.
Configured single-label restore follows below; full automatic publication remains open.

## Configured single-label restore

remote restore --label LABEL --max-bytes N --max-expanded-bytes N resolves
one declared final directory from merged active configuration. Optional
--position source/dest, --provider local/github and --title restrict lookup;
--profile follows existing earlier-profile/local precedence. --remote-version
selects an exact archive version; otherwise numeric newest is selected. GitHub
latest reads canonical VERSION.zip, then downloads its label ZIP. --repository
owner/repo avoids requiring Git; otherwise origin is inspected locally and its
host must match the API. GITHUB_API_URL and existing environment tokens retain
the explicit transport contract. No credentials are installed.

Existing per-directory source.local/source.github title references or named
inline definitions precede eligible build.local/build.github destinations.
A shared referenced definition may be refined inline through the existing deep
merge (null still inherits). Destination source:false excludes it; true or a
matching label preference beats the first eligible fallback. content:null/false
selects nothing, true selects declared non-cache roles, and lists select declared
labels. Source/provider/title declaration order is preserved. No retry switches
to another configured source after lookup/download fails.

A valid root manifest.csv is required, matching projr's prior-build gate.
Labels with no recorded files and advertised empty variants skip without clearing.
CSV history is not used as an integrity/trust proof. Full sources stage before
the existing merge/clear installer; --clear never removes files before a source
has been found and copied. Default merge preserves destination-only files.
Machine results disclose restored/skipped, selected provider/title/version and
destination; failures keep protocol stdout structured with static error text. Stderr carries
the operational diagnostic chain, including paths and parser details; it is not
a general configuration-redaction boundary. HTTP errors omit credentials and
response bodies.

This deliberately fixes R source-selection indexing/inline-definition bugs and
clear-before-lookup data loss. It does not add R's implicit hard-coded archive
fallback: undeclared remotes/paths are errors under the agreed explicit mapping
contract. Nonempty get policy mappings fail explicitly rather than pretending
that R's ineffective get.strategy/get.conflict controls work. Send policy is not
executed by restore. Definitions retain local path versus GitHub title/tag id
semantics, including spaces and @version tag normalization.

Boundary: ordinary inline remote/source fields are accepted by this command's
read-only configuration projection only. Normal build validation still rejects
unsupported ordinary publication fields, preventing silently ignored uploads.
Configured automatic publication, cue/history policy integration, all-label
default restore, complete credential-helper fallback and the issue706 registry
remain subsequent work. Installed preview remains unchanged.

cover source priority, references/inline/profiles, destination preference,

Configured restore uses the shared profile selection order: explicit profile,
PROJR_PROFILE, QUARTO_PROFILE, then build.profile, with earlier profiles winning
and local overrides last. Machine failures preserve installation/recovery details
on stderr, including retained backup paths; stdout stays a structured failure.
Legacy data CSV rows and remote data namespaces are read without rewriting
history; ambiguous canonical/legacy namespaces fail before installation.
One optional VERSION trust marker is accepted; it is not a byte-verification claim.

## Configured local publication candidate

Current source supports build.local archive (the default) and latest publication with manifest inspection
by default, explicit file comparison, or explicit none comparison. This is newer than installed preview.2 and is not complete projr remote
parity. All selected namespace identities are checked before hooks; every current
CSV-selected snapshot and existing remote metadata is staged/read before the
first destination changes. Data precedes manifest.csv, VERSION and an existing
project CHANGELOG.md. The build's existing irreversible publication boundary
preserves the successful local release on publication failure and skips its
next-dev bump; remote effects may be partial.

~~~yaml
build:
  scripts: []
  git: false
  local:
    delivery:
      path: ../delivery
      structure: latest
      content: [output]
      send:
        inspect: file
        cue: if-change
        strategy: sync-diff
~~~

Content false/null selects nothing, true selects declared non-cache labels, and
a list selects exactly those declared labels. Selected labels require CSV hash
capture. Explicit label lists retain order; true uses sorted declared labels.
There is no implicit role/destination and no registry706 change. Previews and
output_run:false skip publication.

| Control | This candidate's execution/fixture scope | Remaining |
|---|---|---|
| Content true/false/null/list | Actual CLI selection fixtures; true excludes cache | Full configured provider matrix |
| cue if-change / always | Both against each strategy; repeated identical sync-diff tests label-version retention/advance | Archive comparison-version selection |
| inspect file | Shared MD5 byte inspection and exact source-byte validation, local/GitHub | Live provider evidence |
| inspect manifest | Default/explicit local/GitHub comparison; matching history and physical fallback | CSV authenticity is not provided |
| inspect none | All four strategies and both cues; default upload-all; exact build/store/restore bytes and trust markers | Other providers/layouts |
| upload-all | Upload all selected files, retain extras; existing remote marked untrusted | Other inspection modes |
| upload-missing | Preserve existing names/bytes, add missing; changes to existing remote marked untrusted | Other inspection modes |
| sync-diff | Add/change/remove; no-change cue fixture | Archive/history interaction |
| sync-purge | Mirror full selected file set, including same-byte files, matching the pinned source quirk | Other inspection modes |

if-change, sync-diff and manifest inspection remain the existing defaults.
Nonempty get controls,
send.conflict and title-level cue are not silently accepted as working policy.
path-append-label:false is explicitly deferred here because its full destination
contains the shared metadata namespace.

History retains prior label/version rows and replaces current label/version rows
with the current project CSV rows. Upload modes can intentionally preserve extra
or old bytes, so desired-source CSV history is not proof that those bytes equal
the remote; the VERSION asterisk discloses untrusted existing state.

Two source defects are corrected explicitly: newly empty latest labels receive
an advertised VERSION entry, and file-equal sync-diff repairs missing/starred
label metadata after inspection. Pinned R latest/file returns the project version
without checking VERSION (.dsl_gr_gvc_latest_file); its no-change branch can
otherwise leave the directory undiscoverable or stale-marked. This is a bounded
metadata/discoverability correction, not a new default cue or trust policy.

Ponytail full shares the existing definition/content parser, numeric version
validation, CSV format and four-strategy actions/guarded installer. Snapshots
preserve selected source directory modes and all staging trees get explicit
cleanup on success/failure. Planned missing-path namespaces use conservative
portable case/NFC comparison; actual native spelling is rechecked before installation.
No ownership/ACL/xattr, crash atomicity or concurrent-writer isolation claim.
No actual GitHub Release test mutation or local heavy testing. Remote exact-head
checks and independent review are required before delivery.


When publishing output-r-data, an existing legacy data/data-empty namespace or
data entry in remote VERSION is rejected. Restore can still read legacy data;
publication does not rename, delete or migrate it. Choose a separate destination
until an explicit migration is supported.


### No comparison during configured local publication

Set send.inspect to none to make planning ignore comparison hashes/history.
The default strategy then becomes upload-all; both cues still upload nonempty
sources. Explicit upload-missing and sync-diff also blindly overwrite selected
filenames and retain remote-only files, matching projr rather than their
file-inspected behavior. Existing destinations are marked untrusted with a star.

Explicit sync-purge replaces the entire file set when the source is nonempty.
With an empty source it retains unknown remote extras: without comparison, projr
does not discover extras to trigger a purge. New empty destinations are still
advertised. These combinations are covered by actual CLI build/store/restore
fixtures, including repeated same-byte builds and both cues.

None controls comparison decisions; guarded path/type checks, source CSV-byte
validation, staging and physical installation safety still read files. It is not
a promise of zero remote reads or hashing. The shared physical transfer remains
guarded and may read destination bytes while installing. Archive and configured
GitHub publication remain pending.


### Manifest comparison for local latest publication

Manifest is the default inspection. The remote label VERSION must be unstarred,
and the corresponding label/version CSV rows must exist and match project history
exactly as filename/MD5 sets. Then current source rows are compared with those
recorded rows. Otherwise comparison falls back to physical files. Missing,
mismatched, duplicate or ambiguous rows cannot establish trust; malformed history
still fails closed rather than being overwritten.

A matching history is a performance/decision trust convention, not proof of
actual remote bytes. If bytes drift independently while history still agrees,
unselected files are retained. Use inspect: file to compare actual bytes.
Sync-purge still replaces the whole file set when triggered. Shared guarded
staging checks physical paths/types/bytes during installation; this mode does not
promise zero remote reads. Explicit upload-all ignores comparison like projr.

Projr strips the star before its latest-manifest helper checks history. Rust
deliberately treats a starred label as untrusted and falls back to file comparison,
consistent with the stated marker meaning. This is a source bug correction, not
a new history/authenticity policy. Archive and configured GitHub publication are
still pending.


### Configured ordinary local archives

Omitting structure uses archive, matching projr. Each label stores complete
snapshots at path/label/vVERSION (or vVERSION-empty), with shared metadata at path.
Earlier versions are retained. Explicit path-append-label:false remains unsupported
for configured publication; source lookup/explicit download support is separate.

For if-change, an older archive can be reused only when its newest catalog entry,
unstarred VERSION label and matching project/remote history agree, and the version
falls within the continuous unchanged suffix of project history. File inspection
then compares that eligible directory's bytes; manifest inspection compares its
recorded rows. Missing/stale/future/mismatched/untrusted evidence forces the current
version. Always with an absent current destination selects a fresh snapshot.
None and upload-all do not select historical comparisons.

When a new snapshot is required it contains the complete current CSV-selected
source, including when only one file differed from an older comparison. This
avoids the native source's potential partial-new-directory behavior after old
comparison byte drift. Old snapshots are never patched as comparison sources.
Shared metadata still advances when unchanged content reuses an older version.
Empty transitions retain history; redundant unchanged empty snapshots are skipped.

Remote fixtures cover the 3 inspection x 4 strategy x 2 cue matrix through actual
build/store/restore, default archive/manifest, empty transitions, reversion after
an intervening change, and missing/untrusted/forward/drifted comparison evidence.
Archive root/container identities and catalogs are validated before hooks; exact
current-version spelling is checked during all-target preparation before any
destination applies. No remote transaction or concurrent-writer guarantee.
Configured GitHub publication and CAS policy remain separate.


### Configured GitHub publication candidate

Current source adds a bounded build.github path:

~~~yaml
build:
  git: false
  scripts: []
  github:
    data:
      content: [output]
      send: {inspect: none}
~~~

Archive is the existing structure default; none inspection defaults upload-all.
Both cues upload selected nonempty bytes without historical comparison. Archive data uses
native label-vVERSION.zip or label-vVERSION-empty.zip names and the existing
prefix/append-label naming. Missing Releases are created as normal published
Releases, not drafts. Use a dedicated destination for testing.

Git origin selects owner/repository; existing API URL and credentials are captured
before hooks. No credentials are installed or changed. Current CSV-selected bytes
stream into restorable ZIPs; all targets stage before the first upload. Existing
CSV/VERSION history is retained. Data precedes manifest.zip, VERSION.zip and an
existing project CHANGELOG.zip. Metadata ZIPs require exactly the canonical member;
shared metadata and existing data download/extraction are bounded at 128 MiB
compressed and expanded per archive; current/newest eligible data is staged privately under that same expanded limit.
Unselected older archives are not downloaded. These caps fail during preparation
before remote changes.

Set structure: latest to replace label.zip (or label-empty.zip). Archive remains
the default and may replace only the exact canonical current-version asset;
older versions remain untouched. Existing data ZIPs are downloaded and validated,
then selected CSV bytes overwrite their matching members while remote-only files
survive. Empty source selection leaves existing data intact; the strategy table below
explains when label VERSION also advances.
Upload-all, upload-missing and sync-diff updates to existing targets receive a
starred VERSION because retained extras are not described by the source inventory.
A nonempty sync-purge replaces the complete file set and removes that star. Project/history
metadata still advances. Empty-to-full upload removes the validated obsolete
empty variant only after the full upload succeeds.

Catalog case/numeric aliases, simultaneous full/empty assets, malformed ZIPs and
legacy data ambiguity fail during all-target preparation before upload/deletion.
File/manifest comparison uses the shared rules below. Data and
shared metadata replacement use non-atomic delete-then-upload: failure may leave partial state
or a missing asset. The successful local release survives and next-dev bump is
skipped. No remote rollback, automatic retry or concurrent-writer isolation claim.

Evidence uses actual CLI build/store/restore against loopback mocked REST,
including Release creation, ZIP members, metadata replacement, old archive
retention, latest replacement/restore with retained extras, both cues, empty-source
preservation, validated empty transitions, partial failure and preflight rejection. This is not a live GitHub
Release round trip. Installed preview unchanged; remote CI/review required.


Non-public API origins require an explicit environment token. Default github.com
Git/gh credential helpers are only used for the standard HTTPS api.github.com
origin (port443), never forwarded to Enterprise/custom hosts. A regression uses
a fake public helper and verifies it is not invoked for a loopback API.


Public gh credential fallback explicitly requests --hostname github.com, so an
inherited GH_HOST cannot select Enterprise credentials for the public API.
Numeric archive alias checks remove exactly one generated .zip suffix, preserving
valid prefixes/labels that themselves end in .zip. Regression fixtures cover both.

### GitHub no-inspection strategy controls

With explicit send.inspect: none, the default strategy is upload-all. All four
strategies are supported with either cue and latest/archive layout:

| Strategy | Nonempty source against existing target | Empty source against existing target |
|---|---|---|
| upload-all | Upload every selected file; retain extras | Keep data and label VERSION |
| upload-missing | Same blind upload as upload-all | Keep data and label VERSION |
| sync-diff | Same blind upload as upload-all | Keep data; advance untrusted label VERSION |
| sync-purge | Replace complete data file set | Keep data and label VERSION |

These are pinned projr's none-inspection interactions: no comparison means every
source file is considered extra, so missing/diff cannot skip existing matching
paths or infer destination-only files. Neither cue changes that fact. Nonempty
purge knows the complete replacement and produces an unstarred label VERSION.
Empty source cannot infer destination extras, even under purge/always.
New targets (including empty targets) remain discoverable as described above.

Mock REST fixtures execute all 2 layouts x 4 strategies x 2 cues through actual
build and configured restore with exact ZIP/metadata/retained-extra assertions;
empty-source coverage checks all strategies and cues. This is not live GitHub
evidence. File/manifest and archive-history rules follow below.


### GitHub file/manifest comparison and archive history

Omitting send uses the existing defaults: inspect: manifest, strategy: sync-diff,
cue: if-change and structure: archive. Explicit file and none are also supported.
All modes use the same ordinary publication planner as local remotes, operating
on private staged GitHub data/metadata before any upload or deletion.

File inspection compares actual uncompressed path/MD5 inventories. Manifest
inspection uses matching project and remote label/version CSV rows only when
VERSION is unstarred; otherwise it falls back to file inspection. Matching CSV
does not authenticate bytes: unselected actual drift survives a trusted partial
sync-diff. Missing/mismatched/starred history cannot establish trust.

For archive comparison, only the newest advertised catalog entry may be reused.
Catalog/version/CSV must agree and the advertised version must lie in the
continuous unchanged suffix of project history. Changed-then-reverted content
cannot reuse a pre-change snapshot. None/upload-all bypass historical comparison;
always with no current target creates a new snapshot. New snapshots contain the
complete current CSV-selected source, including when only part changed relative
to an older comparison. Older archive assets remain untouched.

Current data and an eligible newest historical entry are downloaded and validated
before writes; an ineligible older archive is not downloaded. Ambiguous newest
numeric/full/empty variants and portable aliases fail closed. Empty historical
ZIPs must contain exactly the native zero-byte sentinel, even when CSV agrees.

| GitHub controls | Candidate verification |
|---|---|
| 3 inspections x 4 strategies x 2 cues x 2 layouts | Actual CLI mocked REST data/metadata and restore matrix |
| Archive unchanged/changed history across all 24 control combinations | Complete snapshots, exact VERSION, old bytes preserved |
| Trusted partial manifest / starred, mismatched or missing history | Preserve unselected drift / file fallback |
| Archive reversion, physical drift, ineligible/future metadata | Correct reuse versus complete current snapshot |
| Empty transitions and corrupt empty history | Stage/validate before upload/deletion |
| Live GitHub round-trip | Not performed; requires a dedicated safe destination |

Source-only candidate pending exact-head remote CI and independent review;
